analysis.verdict: Act Financial is an investment company whose profits rise and fall with the Egyptian market, and both its earnings and its share price are falling. It swung from a profit of EGP 1.02bn in the first half of 2025 to a loss of EGP 197.7m in the first half of 2026. The shares are in a downtrend, 30% under their 52-week high and well below the 2024 listing-day levels. There is a short-term bounce from the October low of 1.95, but nothing in the price or the results yet says the decline is over. The tracker rates it HOLD with a negative lean.

p: Act Financial is a Cairo-based investment company founded in 2015 and led by co-founder Bassem Azab. It takes strategic and anchor stakes in listed and private Egyptian companies and aims to profit from their rise in value. Its investments are spread over financial services, pharmaceuticals, building materials, industry and real estate.

It is not an operating business with steady sales. Its reported revenue is mostly gains and losses on the investments it holds or sells, so results swing sharply with the market. A good year on the EGX produces large profits; a bad quarter produces a loss.

2026 has been a poor year. The first quarter showed a loss of EGP 513.1m against a profit of EGP 419.0m a year earlier. The first half showed a loss of EGP 197.7m against a profit of about EGP 1.02bn, with revenue down from EGP 1.22bn to EGP 192.9m and a loss per share of EGP 0.171. The first-half loss being smaller than the first-quarter loss implies a profit of roughly EGP 315m in the second quarter.

The cause was a negative return of EGP 215.6m on investment sales and fair-value changes. Third-quarter results have not been found yet. The market fell sharply in October, which points to further mark-downs in the fourth quarter unless it recovers by year end.

On 10 September 2026 the company agreed to buy commercial and office units in the URBN-K development in New Cairo for EGP 203.4m. Market value is about EGP 2.6bn. I could not find a current net asset value per share, which is the number that matters most for an investment company, so I cannot say whether the shares trade above or below the value of what the company owns.

The shares began trading on 31 July 2024 from a reference price of EGP 2.90 and closed that first day at 3.76. The highest close was 3.70 in November 2024. From there the trend has been down in steps: about 3.00 in mid-2025, 2.81 at the end of 2025, and 2.61 by March 2026.

A rally in September 2026 reached a 52-week high of 3.25 on 20 September and then failed. The price fell to an all-time low of 1.95 on 26 October during the market sell-off. It has since recovered to 2.26 (close of 12 November), 16% above the low and 30% below the high. Annualised volatility is about 33%. Average turnover is about 20m shares or EGP 55m a day, so it is liquid for its size.

The primary trend is down: price (2.26) is below the 50-day average (2.51), which is below the 200-day (2.67). Momentum has turned up in the short term, with MACD above its signal line and RSI back to a neutral 46, which is the pattern of a relief bounce inside a downtrend.
bullets: Support: 1.95 (the 26 October low, also the all-time low). A close below it means new lows with no chart support underneath.
First resistance: 2.51 to 2.54 (the 50-day average and the 20-day high).
Trend resistance: 2.67 (the 200-day average). A close above it would be the first real sign of a turn.

p: At a buy price near 3.4 the shares need to rise about 50% to break even. That would take them above the 52-week high of 3.25 and close to the highest levels since listing. On present evidence that requires both a market recovery and a clear turn in the company's results. The signal here answers a narrower question: whether the trend is improving or worsening from today's price. It does not know your cost and it does not turn positive because a position is under water.

sections.h: What would make it a buy
bullets: A close above the 200-day average (about 2.67) with the 50-day average turning up.
Third-quarter or full-year results back in profit, showing investment gains have returned.
A sustained EGX recovery, since the company's holdings are mostly Egyptian equities.
A disclosed net asset value well above the share price, or a buyback.

sections.h: What would make it a sell
bullets: Another quarterly loss, or large write-downs on holdings.
A further market sell-off or another rate hike.
Heavy selling by major shareholders or a dilutive capital increase.
The central bank's December rate meeting and the direction of the EGX30.
Completion and financing of the EGP 203m New Cairo property purchase.
Disclosures of stakes bought or sold in portfolio companies.
